Then the scalar equation, current, and scalar stress vanish, and the full coupled field equations reduce exactly to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations. Conversely, any smooth source-free Einstein–Maxwell solution on this region that admits the global potential $F=dA$ is a solution of the defined charged-scalar system with $\varphi=0$. The condition $V(0)=0$ is essential for the zero scalar stress conclusion. In particular, source-free initial data in this exact-potential sector that satisfy the local-development theorem's hypotheses have a smooth local realization in this branch.

1.3 First propagate the magnetic residual $U:=dF$, independently of the scalar equation and current. The normal evolution gives $\iota_nU=0$, so a three-form decomposition in an adapted frame gives $U=q\,\iota_n\mathrm{vol}_g$. Its pullback to the initial slice is $(D_ib^i)\mathrm{vol}_h=0$, hence $q=0$ initially. Since $dU=d^2F=0$, the coordinate volume formula gives $
abla_a(qn^a)=n(q)+q
abla_an^a=0$. On each normal integral curve the integrating factor $\exp(\int
abla_an^a)$ makes $q$ constant times its initial value, so $q=0$ near the initial slice. Thus $dF=0$ before any current-conservation or Einstein inference. The normal is transverse to the time levels and its local flow exists with unique curves; at the stated finite Sobolev regularity it is at least $C^1$. [given, L5, L7, L8, L13, L14, A1, A2, algebra]

4.1 Put $W:=d\star_gF-\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$. Its normal contraction vanishes by the sourced evolution, so $W=r\,\iota_n\mathrm{vol}_g$. Initially, the Hodge formula in [L7] gives $(\star_gF)|_\Sigma=\iota_e\mathrm{vol}_h$, while $(\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)|_\Sigma=j^0\mathrm{vol}_h$. Thus $W|_\Sigma=(D_ie^i-\mu_0j^0)\mathrm{vol}_h=0$. By [L8] and step 3.1, $dW=-\mu_0(\nabla_aj^a)\mathrm{vol}_g=0$. The same normal-volume computation as step 1.3 gives $n(r)+r\nabla_an^a=0$ with zero initial value, and the integrating factor proves $r=0$. Thus the full sourced Maxwell equation holds, with the divergence sign established in step 3.1. For the classical finite-Sobolev solutions, these identities also hold distributionally; the continuous residuals and their initial traces give the same zero solution in the $C^1$ normal flow coordinates. [given, L5, L7, L8, L13, A1, A2, step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]
